findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses a hash dictionary self.videos for active video records, a min-heap self.available_ids for recycled deleted IDs, and a counter self.next_id for new IDs. Operations upload, remove, watch, like, dislike, getLikesAndDislikes, and getViews execute in optimal O(log Q + C) time and O(U + Q) space; no candidate is required.

Upload pops from available_ids min-heap when non-empty, otherwise uses next_id, guaranteeing smallest available ID reuse. Remove deletes from self.videos (if present) and pushes the ID to available_ids. Watch clamps endMinute to string length and increments view count. Statistic methods handle missing IDs with sentinels [-1], -1, and '-1'.

Heap upload/remove operations take O(log Q) time. Watch takes O(C) for returning C characters. Overall time complexity across Q operations is O(Q log Q + C) with O(U + Q) space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Implements all VideoSharingPlatform methods with accurate ID assignment, view clamping, statistics tracking, and missing-video sentinels.

The approach accurately details separating active content from reusable IDs, heap ID management, and O(Q log Q + C) time / O(U + Q) space complexity. Alternatives and edge cases cover scanning for gaps, search trees, monotone counters, repeated removals, ID reuse resetting statistics, watch range clamping, missing ID sentinels, and counter independence.
